newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault says 1996 op. loss to exceed mkt forecast.
newsitem.headline: Renault says 1996 op. loss to exceed mkt forecast.

text.p: French carmaker Renault issued a warning on Friday that its 1996 operating loss would be "considerably higher" than the market generally reckoned because of a difficult economic climate.

"In view of the prevailing economic context, and despite the increase in revenues of the automobile division, reflecting a more positive trend which has been confirmed by a widening of the Renault market share in France in the early part of 1997, the operating loss to be reported by Renault Group for 1996 will be considerably higher than that generally anticipated by the financial markets," Renault said in a statement.
The company has previously issued profit warnings for 1996, saying both its car and truck operations would lose money.

One analyst said the market had been expecting an operating loss of roughly two billion francs for the car division, an operating loss of around 600 million francs for the trucks and an operating profit of around 1.3 billion at the finance unit, for a total operating loss of 1.3 billion francs.
He said he expected the car division's loss to be nearer 2.8 billion francs after the profit warning.
